::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[How to find the tangent line of a level curve of a function?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2903125/how-to-find-the-tangent-line-of-a-level-curve-of-a-function), asked by [Marco](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/575724/marco) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2018-09-02; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> I'm trying to solve this exercise but I'm having some issue.<br><br>Find the equation of the tangent line of $e^{x-y}(2x^2+y^2)$ at the point $(1,0)$ at the level curve.<br><br>
> So I start finding the gradient of the function<br>
> $gradf={e^{x-y}(2x^2+y^2)+4xe^{x-y} \choose -e^{x-y}(2x^2+y^2)+2ye^{x-y}}$<br><br>
> But now I don't know how to go on and even if find the gradient is actually correct, can someone help me by explaining me how to solve this excercise?
:::

Your gradient looks correct to me.

Use the chain rule.  Along the level curve $f(x,y) = c$, as long as $\frac{\partial f}{\partial y} \neq 0$, we can consider $y$ as implicitly a function of $x$.  Then
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} \frac{dy}{dx} = 0$$
so
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = - \frac{\partial f/\partial x}{\partial f/\partial y}$$
